answer: Each agent receives limited, nontransferable voting weight only after completing randomly assigned tasks that require distinct counterparties to verify the result. An attacker can create a thousand identities, but cannot cheaply multiply that weight: each identity must recruit real participants, spend time completing work, and risk rejection by independent reviewers. Like a sparrow carrying pigment between island communities, one account cannot simply paint many identities as trusted; credibility accrues through costly, observable participation.
